draft.title: International environmental agreements
card: An international environmental agreement is a treaty between countries. It sets shared goals for a problem that crosses borders.
a treaty on climate change. Each country sets its own targets to cut greenhouse gas emissions and reports on its progress.
a treaty to protect the variety of living things, use biological resources sustainably and share their benefits fairly.

A country is bound only if it chooses to join the treaty. Most treaties have no world police force, so they rely on countries keeping their own promises. Pressure from other countries and public reporting can encourage compliance.
draft.remember: Environmental treaties set shared goals, but they mostly depend on each country keeping its word.

a.q: Why do most international environmental agreements depend on countries keeping their own promises?
opts: There is no world police force to make countries comply
Treaties are not binding on any country that joins them
Each treaty is enforced by the courts of one country
Treaties only cover problems inside a single country
a.why: Most treaties have no global body that can force countries to act, so they rely on each country to follow through. The option saying treaties never bind is wrong: a country that joins takes on the commitment, but nothing forces it to keep it.
a.clue: Think about who could force a country to act.

b.q: Country X joins the Paris Agreement and sets its own target to cut emissions. Years later it is well short of that target. What best describes the agreement's position?
opts: It relies on pressure and reporting, not direct enforcement
It lets a world court seize the country's factories
It automatically cancels the country's membership
It sets the same fixed target for every country
b.why: The Paris Agreement relies on countries setting their own targets and reporting progress, so the main tools are pressure and public reporting. The option about a fixed target for all countries is tempting but wrong, because each country sets its own.
b.clue: Recall who sets the targets and what happens to a country that falls short.

a.best: There is no world police force to make countries comply

b.best: It relies on pressure and reporting, not direct enforcement
